findings.title: Hazard list omits the .faff/anchors/* and .faff/anchors/** family
findings.action: Fold the anchors-targeted spellings into FAFF-1301's git-asking predicate, or narrow the residual-limitation claim.
findings.disposition_rationale: Confirmed real empirically: a root `.faff/anchors/**` leaves `.faff/.gitignore` readable yet `git check-ignore -v` attributes the anchor file to `.gitignore:1:.faff/anchors/**`, and the writer reports warnings: []. Out of this slice's spec'd scope (the DONE list fixes an eight-entry floor and explicitly admits a wider list). Recorded as discovered scope and flagged as evidence for FAFF-1301, whose predicate asks git instead of enumerating spellings and so catches this class by construction. see <run-dir>/FAFF-1299/discovered-scope.json

findings.finding_id: plugin/skills/faff/bin/lib/gitignore-ensure.js::appended /* can land after a pre-existing negation and kill the carve-out
findings.title: Appended /* can land after a pre-existing negation and kill the carve-out
findings.action: Detect a negation at a lower index than where /* would land and warn, reusing the new warning machinery; reordering is unavailable because append-only is a hard constraint.
findings.disposition_rationale: Confirmed real empirically and worse than described: seeding `.faff/.gitignore` with only `!/anchors/` yields an output whose `/*` sits at line 4 after the negation at line 1, and git attributes the ignored anchor file to `.faff/.gitignore:4:/*`. The writer thus produces a file defeating the carve-out the ticket protects. Not fixed here: the trigger needs a hand-written partial file that no faff-managed repo contains (the writer always emits the complete ordered set), the spec's DONE list is complete without it, and the only append-only-compatible remedy is a new warning, which is a behaviour addition rather than a correction of what was specified. Recorded as discovered scope at the top of the list. see <run-dir>/FAFF-1299/discovered-scope.json

findings.finding_id: plugin/skills/faff/bin/lib/gitignore-ensure.js::hazard scan ignores .git/info/exclude, which faff's own --local mode writes .faff/ into
findings.title: Hazard scan ignores .git/info/exclude, which faff's own --local mode writes .faff/ into
findings.action: Scan .git/info/exclude when present, or document the local-to-standard transition as a known gap.
findings.disposition_rationale: Confirmed real empirically: after a `--local` run writes `.faff/` to `.git/info/exclude`, a standard run reports warnings: [] while git attributes the ignored anchor file to `.git/info/exclude:14:.faff/`. Reachable and tool-created, not a residual unlisted spelling. Out of this slice's spec'd scope (hazard detection is specified over the root .gitignore). Recorded as discovered scope; FAFF-1301's git-asking predicate is immune to it. see <run-dir>/FAFF-1299/discovered-scope.json

findings.action: Add the half-applied row to the spec's edge-case table if completeness is claimed.
findings.disposition_rationale: Accepted, and the reviewer concedes acceptability in the finding itself: a throw on the second write exits 2, which signals the half-applied state, and the operation is idempotent so a re-run converges. findings.finding_id: plugin/skills/faff/bin/lib/gitignore-ensure.js::hazard warning text claimed inaccurate for the partial-hazard family
findings.title: Hazard warning text claimed inaccurate for the partial-hazard family
findings.action: None required; the premise is incorrect.
findings.refutation: gitignore-ensure.js:155-158 reads "Git will not read .faff/.gitignore, or will keep ignoring files under the directories it re-includes". The text is a disjunction whose second clause states precisely the partial-hazard behaviour.
findings.disposition_rationale: The finding's premise is that the warning asserts non-reading unconditionally. It does not: the sentence is an explicit either-or covering both the full and partial families, which is why one remedy serves both. A finding that contradicts the source it cites loses to the source.

findings.action: Acknowledge in the text that a **/-prefixed match may be intentional elsewhere in the tree.
findings.disposition_rationale: Fair usability point and accepted as such.
